question.text: Both lithium and magnesium display several similar properties due to the diagonal relationship; however, the one which is incorrect is:

options.text: Nitrates of both <math> <semantics> <mrow> <mtext>L</mtext><mtext>i</mtext> </mrow> </semantics> </math> and <math> <semantics> <mrow> <mtext>M</mtext><mtext>g</mtext> </mrow> </semantics> </math> yield <math><mtext>N</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>O</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mtext>O</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> on heating

solution.text: Carbonate of magnesium is basic, sometimes appears as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>MgCO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>.</mo><mi>Mg</mi><msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>OH</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></math> but that of lithium is not basic.
